messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>

Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>

Subject: Follow-up: hosting mode clarification + EU/APAC routing constraints

Hi Lina / AcmeFin team,

Thanks again for taking the time today — wanted to capture the key items from our call and proposed next steps so we all stay aligned. Short TL;DR at top, details below.

TL;DR
- Production must be EU-only for customer data (data-at-rest + inference processing).
- APAC users will be primarily read-only but may have low-volume inference requests (latency-sensitive).
- Primary options: Hosted (eu region) vs Dedicated (reserved GPU in EU) vs Private (VPC) — tradeoffs below.

Notes from the call
- Residency requirement: Production inference + logs must remain in EU; dev/staging can reside outside EU if necessary but customer prefers dev in EU when possible.
- Encryption: You asked about customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM). Hosted API supports service-managed KMS today; Dedicated and Private can integrate with customer-managed KMS (we'll confirm HSM options).
- Cross-region routing: You asked whether requests from APAC can be routed to EU region without traversing US egress points. For Hosted we route regionally (eu-west silo) but we need to confirm network egress topology for APAC mobile clients. Private (VPC) gives you full control over egress.
- Logging & retention: We discussed retention windows and audit logs; will provide SOC2 summary and network diagram.

Proposed next steps (please confirm):
1) Neha to share SOC2 summary + network diagram (attached).
2) Technical deep-dive (60m) with your infra/security team to walk residency, KMS, and egress flow. Rafael to propose times.
3) If Hosted looks sufficient, propose a small POC in our EU region (3-4k tokens/day) to validate routing and latency from APAC. If not, scope Dedicated vs Private.
4) Provide list of specific endpoints/clients and expected qps from APAC so we can size Dedicated or suggest edge strategy.

Attachments: SOC2_Summary_AcmeFin.pdf, Residency_Requirements_AcmeFin.xlsx (draft).

If you want to add anything I missed, reply inline. Otherwise, I can propose 2 windows for the deep-dive tomorrow/Thursday.

Best,
Rafael

- Confirmed: production inference must only process and persist EU data (we cannot have any customer PII leave the EU).
- For APAC: our user base is mostly APAC/SEA. We anticipate bursty traffic (spikes during business hours) but most volumes are low. Latency matters for certain UX flows (sub-300ms ideal).
- KMS: we strongly prefer customer-managed keys for production. If Hosted cannot support CMK in the short term, we need clear timelines.

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Follow-up: hosting mode clarification + EU/APAC routing constraints

Hi Lina — looping in a few technical detail points so your security/infra folks have something concrete ahead of the deep-dive. Attaching SOC2 summary and a simple network diagram.

Short answers first:
- Can Hosted keep processing in EU? Yes — our Hosted API has a dedicated eu-west region (physical compute and storage located in the EU) and we can pin customer production workloads to that region so inference + logs remain in-region.
- Customer-managed KMS (CMK): Hosted (shared) does not currently support CMK integration out-of-the-box. Dedicated reserved capacity and Private VPC deployments do support CMK (and can be configured to use a customer HSM depending on deployment). Timeline: CMK for Hosted is on our roadmap but not available in the near term (we can share roadmap notes under NDA).
- APAC edge fronting: Fronting via an edge (CDN/anycast) is possible for TLS termination and faster client handshake, but note that if you route from APAC -> edge -> eu-hosted, the actual inference traffic flows to EU compute (so processing stays in EU). The network egress path (carrier/anycast handoffs) may touch non-EU networks briefly; that can be acceptable for non-PII but your policy says PII must not leave EU — so we should review specific traffic flows and client-side handling.

Tradeoffs summary: 
- Hosted (EU region): fastest path to POC, lower ops overhead, but no CMK today. Good if EU residency + service-managed keys are acceptable.
- Dedicated (EU reserved): Dedicated GPU pools in the EU, supports CMK, better isolation and predictable throughput; higher cost and lead time to provision.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): Full control over networking, egress, and keys; best for strict data-sovereignty + integration needs; longest procurement and ops commitment.

Requested items for deep-dive:
1) A list of endpoints (mobile/web) and expected p95 latency requirement.
2) Examples of PII fields we must treat as EU-only.
3) Any corporate egress restrictions or network allowlists.

Attachments included: SOC2_Summary_AcmeFin.pdf, network-diagram.pdf.

Next: Rafael will propose two windows and we can lock one for a focused technical call with our infra team (EMEA-friendly time).

Cheers,
Neha Kapoor
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Great — thanks for the quick replies and for confirming constraints, Lina. Based on Neha's note, here's a recommended path and calendar options.

Recommended short path (fastest to validate):
1) POC in Hosted EU region (eu-west) with service-managed keys to validate latency and routing from APAC clients. Goal: measure p95 latency from your APAC test clients and validate that processing and logs remain in EU. Timeline: 1-2 weeks to spin up test tokens.
2) If CMK is a hard requirement for production, run parallel scoping for Dedicated (EU reserved) or Private (VPC) — Neha will scope feasibility & cost during the deep-dive.

Why this order: Hosted POC lets us validate whether APAC fronting + EU processing meets your latency window without the procurement overhead of Dedicated/Private. If it fails due to CMK or egress policy, we move to Dedicated/Private.

Action items / proposed owners:
- Rafael: schedule the technical deep-dive (60m). Proposed windows: 2026-08-14 09:00-10:00 BST or 2026-08-14 15:00-16:00 BST. Please confirm which works for your infra team.
- AcmeFin: send list of sample endpoints, PII fields, and expected p95 latency (per Neha's checklist).
- Neha: bring engineering notes about CMK options and Dedicated sizing.
- Redwood: share SOC2 summary + network diagram (attached).

Links: HubSpot deal (https://app.hubspot.com/deals/5678123) — I will update stage to "POC - Residency validation" once we confirm the call.

If it helps, we can also provide a short write-up comparing Dedicated vs Private costs for EU-only deployments — Grace will draft and share after the call.

Thanks again — looking forward to locking the call and moving to a scoped POC.
